protocol.name: ambrosia_glass_v1

description.summary: glass behind parts of a surface

protocol.description:
Lets a client say which parts of a surface are panes of glass, and of which material each is. The compositor draws what is behind each pane through that material (blurred, saturated, bent at the rim) under the surface; the client draws the tint, the rim and its content on top.
Where a surface has a glass object, its panes replace any blur region the surface asks for by another protocol.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: the manager is no longer needed

request.description: Glass objects made from it live on.

request.name: get_glass
request.description: A surface has one glass object at a time; asking for a second while the first lives replaces the first's panes with the second's, when the surface is next committed.

interface.name: ambrosia_glass_v1

description.summary: the panes of glass in one surface

interface.description: The list of panes is double-buffered state: clear and add_pane build the next list, and it replaces the current one when the surface is next committed.

enum.name: material
enum.description: How much the pane blurs and saturates what is behind it. The values are the compositor's (the design's tokens).

entry.name: backdrop
entry.summary: a blur only, behind content that carries its own glass

request.name: destroy

description.summary: the surface has no glass any more

request.description: The panes go when the surface is next committed. A surface destroyed before that keeps them to its end.

description.summary: start the next list of panes empty

request.name: add_pane

description.summary: add a pane to the next list

request.description: A rounded rectangle in surface-local coordinates, seen only inside the clip rectangle (the same rectangle when nothing clips it). Opacity is 0 to 1: how much of the glass shows, for a pane that is fading in or out. A material the compositor does not know is drawn as regular.
